dedupe_keys.name: derms rt distributed energy resource management using real time optimisation

description: DERMS-RT is a distributed energy resource management solution that uses real-time optimisation to control many kinds of devices on a distribution grid. It is registered on DOE CODE by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory with Fei Ding as developer (software record SWR-20-46, released September 2021), and builds on real-time optimal power flow and distributed control methods developed earlier at NREL. It controls rooftop solar, battery storage, HVAC loads, electric water heaters and electric vehicle charging to provide distribution voltage regulation and peak demand management, in coordination with central utility management systems. An application programming interface extracts grid model information from open-source power system simulation software, solves the optimisation and applies optimal setpoints, giving a plug-and-play way to test real-time DER control on different utility models and a simulation test bed for its effect on grid operations. Coverage is not tied to a place. The DOE CODE record lists it as closed source, so access is on request from NREL, and cost and terms are not stated. Caveats: no public code, documentation or maturity information was found. Simulation uses are distribution voltage control and peak management studies with high DER shares. Related records: model-virtual-battery-aggregator is an open NREL DERMS component.
inputs: Distribution grid model from open-source simulation software
name: DERMS-RT - distributed energy resource management using real-time optimisation
outputs: Optimal DER setpoints for voltage regulation and peak demand management
